The readings by group, their cadence, their warnings, and what an unmeasured reading means.

Sensors

A sensor is one reading of the colony with a fixed name, a type (number, boolean or list) and a catalogue entry that says where it comes from, what it means and when it warns. The Sensors tab shows them all; read_state returns them.

Cadence

CadenceEveryReadings
fastscanclock, pause state, the crew's positions and drafted state, hostiles, letters, alerts
normal4th scanstores, zones, buildings, designations, rooms, power, animals, weapons, research, mood
slow16th scanwealth, damaged buildings, the world map

A reading is taken once per scan and cached, so a ladder of four hundred rungs costs the same as one.

Readings on demand

Three families of key are measured only when a rung names them, so the catalogue never has to list every definition in every mod:

KeyReads
count_<ThingDef>items: the total stack count on the map; buildings: how many stand
research_<ProjectDef>whether that research project is finished (measured for every loaded project)
alert_<AlertClass>whether that alert is active (alert_HunterLacksRangedWeapon, alert_ColonistNeedsRescue)

A definition the game has not loaded leaves the key unmeasured.

Unmeasured

A reading the game cannot give is absent. It is never zero, never false. A rung whose condition names it shows that contact amber and stays quiet. This is deliberate: a guessed zero would make "no freezer" look like "freezer at 0 C" and fire the wrong rung.

A sensor can also be catalogued not-measured: the name is reserved and rungs may read it, but no code writes it yet. The Sensors tab lists those under the inputs nothing is writing.

Warnings

Every catalogue entry carries a label, a group, a tooltip and a severity, and most carry a warn rule -- a boolean rule for a boolean reading, an operator rule for a number. When the rule holds the reading is listed in the warnings panel at the top of the Sensors tab, amber for a warning and red for a critical one. Critical warnings also raise an alert in RimWorld's own alert column: an unarmed colonist, a colonist never set up, an unread threat letter.

Letters

letters counts letters on the stack not yet marked seen. threat_letter is true while a raid or threat letter (ThreatBig / ThreatSmall) is on the stack and recent, and for as long as one is unread, whatever its age -- an unread threat never ages out of the ladder. threat_letter_unread is that last part on its own, and it is critical. The window's Letters seen button, or the letters_seen command, marks the stack read.

RimPLC. A development build; nothing here is a balance, performance or compatibility report.
